text: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound,
to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,

to provide for those who mourn in Zion—to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a faint spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, for his glory.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and raise up what was long devastated; they will restore the ruined cities, desolate for generation after generation.
Strangers will stand and pasture your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers.
But you will be called priests of the LORD; they will speak of you as ministers of our God. You will feed on the wealth of the nations, and in their glory you will boast.

Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of disgrace they will shout for joy over their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess a double portion; everlasting joy will be theirs.

versions.text: Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of disgrace they will rejoice in their inheritance. Therefore in their land they will possess a double portion; everlasting joy will be theirs.
versions.explanation: Hebrew chelqam is 'portion,' the same idea echoed by 'double portion' in the following line; 'inheritance' introduces a different term (nachalah) and breaks the verbal link. 'Shout for joy' also better captures the verb ranan and reads more vividly aloud.

text: For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and wrongdoing. I will faithfully give them their reward and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring will be known among the nations, their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge that they are the offspring the LORD has blessed.

versions.text: Their offspring will be known among the nations, their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads zera' ('seed, offspring'), the same word rendered 'offspring' at the start of the verse. Rendering it 'a people' obscures the deliberate repetition that frames the verse and shifts the sense from lineage to nation.

text: I will rejoice greatly in the LORD; my soul will exult in my God. For he has clothed me with the garments of salvation and wrapped me in the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom wears his priestly headdress, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
For as the earth brings forth its growth, and as a garden causes what is sown to spring up, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
